events.label: discovery
events.text: Peter Skene Ogden's brigade first noted the City of Rocks

evidence.quote: In 1826 , Peter Skene Ogden and his Snake River brigade of beaver trappers were the first Euro-Americans to note

events.label: landmark
events.text: City of Rocks became a landmark for emigrants on the California Trail

evidence.quote: Beginning in 1843 , City of Rocks was a landmark for emigrants on the California Trail
until 1843 , when growing streams of wagons began flowing through the area

events.label: designation
events.text: Idaho Legislature declared Section 36 a state park under Land Board jurisdiction

evidence.quote: a state park under the jurisdiction of the Idaho Land Board on February 27 , 1957

events.label: designation
events.text: A much larger area was designated a National Historic Landmark

evidence.quote: In 1964 , a much larger area ( more than ) was designated a National Historic Landmark

events.label: transfer
events.text: Section 36 transferred to Idaho Department of Parks and Recreation from Department of Lands

evidence.quote: On March 15 , 1973 , Section 36 was transferred to the Idaho Department of Parks and Recreation

events.label: designation
events.text: The area was designated a National Natural Landmark

evidence.quote: The following year , the area was designated a National Natural Landmark

events.label: co-management
events.text: NPS and IDPR begin co-managing the Reserve

evidence.quote: Between 1988 and 1996 , the Reserve was co-managed by both NPS and IDPR

events.label: founding
events.text: Reserve created by Public Law 100-696, Arizona-Idaho Conservation Act of 1988

evidence.quote: City of Rocks National Reserve was created November 18 , 1988 by Public Law 100-696
led to its designation as City of Rocks National Reserve in 1988

events.label: co-management
events.text: NPS and IDPR co-management period ends

evidence.quote: Between 1988 and 1996 , the Reserve was co-managed by both NPS and IDPR

events.label: transfer
events.text: NPS transfers on-site management of the Reserve to IDPR

evidence.quote: the NPS officially transferred on-site management of the Reserve to IDPR on May 2 , 1996

undated_mentions: 1840s-1850s: wagon trains passed through the area on the California Trail
1980s: some of the most difficult climbing routes in the country developed in the area
late 19th century: settlers began to homestead the area
1920s-1930s: dryland farming declined during drought years
mid-19th century: livestock grazing began in the area
1970s-80s: National Park Service studied the site as a proposed national monument
